Perfection's special, Self Transfiguration, is a mode swap (like Lucky Coward's Helping Hand), meaning it serves to change fundamental mechanics of the character or their skills. In this case, Self Transfiguration transitions the player through 3 modes. The standard order is: Fist Blade Club fist Each of the modes works as follows:
Standard 3-3-4-4 M1 string Standard Chase (Honored One, Vessel, etc.) Access to base Focus Strike and its timed variant
Faster 2-2-3-3 Blade M1 string Teleporting Chase (Similar to Salaryman's Blunt Cut) Access to Chainwhip
Slower 4-4-5-5 Club M1 string with 50% damage through block on the 1st and 2nd M1 and block bypassing on the 3rd and 4th M1 Slower, block bypassing Chase Access to Homerun

Perfection has the ability to switch modes in neutral with no restrictions other than an approximate 1/3rd of a second for the switch to happen. Thus, Perfection may use this to his advantage. For example: Switching from Fist to Blade then instantly using Chainwhip to catch the opponent off guard Switching from Fist to Blade mode then using the Blade Chase to catch the opponent off guard or punish an endlag Switching from Fist to Blade in an M1 trade when side dash goes off cooldown to prepare a faster side dash M1 Switching from Fist to Blade on the 3rd Fist M1 for a faster downslam Switching From Blade to Club mode on the 2nd or 3rd M1 to utilize the Club M1's block bypass Switching from Blade to Club then side dashing followed up by a Chase to catch opponents off guard Switching from Club to Fist to catch the opponent with a Chase or punish endlag using it Switching from Club to Fist on the 3rd Club M1 for a faster downslam

Puppet Master can be simplified as a pressure cooker, in which his kit revolves around swarming the opponent with his puppets. His unique [color=#4dd2ff]Offload[/color] special allows him to have variants on 3(basically 4) of his base moves and a new move without consuming the move's cooldown and remaining safe. Both Puppet Barrage and Offloaded Ultra Cannon are pressure tools that force opponents to block. Offloaded Ultra Spin and Heat Emission are both neutral tools that can force an opening for a combo, while all other moves like Boost On can be used at any point in a combo to extend. Using the special while it's still on cooldown will instead use [color=#c3063c]Übercharge[/color]. Puppet Master can still use his offloaded moves except Puppet Barrage in this state, but the move will be put on cooldown upon use while requiring 10% of his ultimate bar to use. While this drains a lot of ultimate bar and removes some of his tools for pressure, this can also reward Puppet Master with higher damage in his comboes. Overall, Puppet Master is a very strong character with an abundance of tools at his disposal for any given scenario in a fight. With enough range and safety from his moves, he is one of the top characters in Jujutsu Shenanigans, and will be hard to fight against if even a single hit lands.

Puppet Master general strategy is to use his moves and special to swarm and overload the opponent with pressure in different ways, whether that's to use certain moves to close in for M1s, punishing mistakes, or to keep an opponent at bay with range. If played properly, the opponent is at a disadvantage due to dealing with the threats of both the Puppet Master and the puppets, allowing for easier conversions into comboes. During the start of a game, the first goal is to get around 20-30% of your ultimate bar so you can comfortably start doing the techs Puppet Master has. This can be adjusted higher depending per player.

Use Heat Emission (non use twice) after they've wasted side dash (its both uncounterable and unblockable). Do Offloaded Ultra Spin into front dash after they've wasted side dash if your 4 isn't up or you wanna save it, they're forced to pick which one they wanna block. Both Puppet Barrage and Offloaded Ultra Cannon apply crazy pressure and forces them to block, basically free m1s if they don't track you well enough. Boost On can surprise people during M1 trades if you do M1 > Boost On instead of M1 x2, but don't expect this to work more than once or twice on competent players. Offloaded Ultra Spin is also a very useful interruption tool to punish opponents who don't bother to block it after they evasive or try to attempt their combo on the player.

Puppet Master can get a free combo off of basically any stray hit, so you're better off freestyling in all honesty. Puppet Master can land an uppercut after Offloaded Ultra Spin, so he can sneak some of those in for an extra 4 damage after Offloaded Ultra Spin. You can use this combo as a template and edit it around as you wish: if you're unable to do the uppercut then its fine to skip it, it's just there for an extra 4 damage M1 M1 M1 UPPERCUT OFFLOADED ULTRA SPIN UPPERCUT (optional) BOOST ON HEAT EMISSION ULTRA SPIN OFFLOADED ULTRA SPIN CHARGED ULTRA CANNON
These require a bit more effort to do compared to the combo in general strategy, tends to use at least one tech listed in the Tech section. (will be moved to the combo section at a later date)

An extremely strong and versatile combo. Do keep in mind this requires you to stall for your offloaded to be AT LEAST halfway ish towards being off cd. You can make a bunch of different variants of this combo pretty easily. You can do this combo with only one R3 at the start for a quadruple instead if you cant afford to save offload. Note

A variant of the quintuple beam. This one works fine with only one R3 at the start as well. You have three different routes to do over 40+ evasiveless damage with Puppet Master. I recommend learning the triple drill first before trying the others as it's by far the most consistent. The triple drill was found by Juno btw thanks Juno. M1 M1 Offloaded Ultra Spin M1 ULTRA SPIN OFFLOADED ULTRA SPIN BOOST ON/ANY VARIANT OF HEAT EMISSION (OPTIONAL) Use ultra spin as late as possible without dropping the combo, it HAS to grab them right after offloaded ultra spin lets go of them. TECH HOW DO I DO THIS NONSENSE WHY IS THIS USEFUL [color=#d11010]Uberstacking[/color] R > Wait for the aura to flare up (takes about .4 seconds or something) > Any skill with an offload variant (1, 3, 4) > R into the same skill immediately One of the most important techs to learn with Puppet Master if you plan to utilize his entire kit. [color=#dc143c]Barrage Stacking (Offloaded)[/color] RR > R1/R4 right as the puppets dash Evasiveless damage is always nice to have. [color=#c0e8f2]Barrage Stacking (Base)[/color] Same thing as offloaded barrage stacking but with a base move instead. RR > 1/4. If you're doing it with 2, hold block and do it after the puppets grab them. If with charged 3, use it right after you do RR and pray. Evasiveless damage is always nice to have. [color=hsl(39, 100%, 50%)]Heat Emission Air M1s[/color] 4 > Land on top of them and start M1ing. A bit difficult to pull off intentionally but if you happen to land on top of them after Heat Emission then the extra damage is very convenient. [color=#00ffe1]Puppet Barrage Air M1s[/color] RR > Hold block and go on top of them after the puppets grab them > Surf on their head and M1 them in the air REALLY INCONSISTENT, but again, the extra damage is very convenient. [color=#8a0e00]4 4 Juggle[/color] M1 the air x2 > Heat Emission use twice variant > Uppercut Mostly used if you wanna confirm into Charged Ultra Cannon, otherwise it does the same damage as regular Heat Emission. Use it combined with [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] during neutral to catch people off guard (granted this eats up your cd) Use this after 3 m1s into an [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] for safety if they have evasive up Uppercut into [i]Ultra Spin[/i] combined with an [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] or another move.

Uppercut into [i]Ultra Spin[/i] combined with an [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] is also decent for evasive baiting as they're likely not expecting the puppet and get hit by it when they attempt to punish you (R1 has a diabolical hitbox). I wouldn't recommend doing this against someone competent though. You can combo extend using this move with anything that sends them into the air (uppercut, R1, R4, very rarely R3) or on wakeup with [i]Boost On[/i] (i wouldn't recommend this tho)

You can use this during neutral to either force out a side dash or block while you do literally anything else. You can follow it up with front dash, side dash [i]Boost On[/i], [i]Heat Emission[/i], or even side dash M1. You can do [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] after an uppercut or 3 m1s into literally any move, though generally speaking you'll follow up with [i]Ultra Spin[/i] into another [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] followed up by anything. Using [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] after [i]Ultra Spin[/i], [i]Boost On[/i], [i]Ultra Cannon[/i], or [i]Offloaded Ultra Cannon[/i] is an effective way to combo extend with [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i].

Using [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] after [i]Boost On[/i] is an effective way to evasive bait as they're forced to eat at least 21.5 damage otherwise if they don't. You can do 3 M1s > [i]Ultra Spin[/i] > Delayed [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] to bait evasive as well. If ever you happen to lose an engagement, if you used [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] before you got hit then they'll automatically lose the engagement if they aren't fast enough to block it while still M1ing you or use a move that gives them some form of iframes.

This move is true and unpunishable after an M1. You can do 3 M1s > [i]Boost On[/i] > [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] to bait out evasive easily. This move can be used when the opponent is ragdolled; be warned though, as this is VERY punishable. If they don't have a counter, you can try timing it right as they get up so they can't react and evasive. Due to it's reactable windup, this is mostly used for combo filler

You side dash, therefore you [i]Boost On[/i]... In all seriousness, despite the move mostly being combo filler, you can use use it with [i]Puppet Barrage[/i] as it forces them to block. Competent players are likely to learn from this and just side dash/front dash away from you before blocking though. You can cheese M1 trades with this similar to how you would use Honored One [i]Rapid Punches[/i] in an M1 trade. Since you're considered airborne at the end of this move, you're vulnerable to both Head of Hei's Decisive Strikes and Defense Attorney's Grapple if they immediately evasive. While you can block Decisive Strikes, you can't with Defense Attorney's Grapple. Make sure you use this move while the Defense Attorney's Justice Served/evasive is on cooldown, as Grapple is a true ragdoll and can start Defense Attorney's pressure. warning!!

This move is strictly combo filler; you can't start a combo with it outside of with [i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] because it's best used at range, and it's 360 blockable. It can, and mostly is used to stall for cooldowns during a combo, or to do a quick burst of damage quickly when combined with [color=#d11010] Uberstacking[/color] (refer to the [color=hsl(39, 100%, 50%)]Techs[/color] and [color=#ff0000]Combos[/color] section of [url=https://dogslamloop.com/characters/Puppet_master/index.html] Overview & Strategy[/url])

Although reacting to [i]Ultra Cannon[/i] by itself is rather simple, pairing it with an [i]Offloaded Ultra Cannon[/i] can create a mixup opportunity where players usually block the first shot but not the follow up from the cannon puppet. You can evasive bait with this move to a certain extent by holding it down and cancelling it right before it becomes charged to fool them into thinking you're leaving yourself open to being punished, albeit this is quite risky. I recommend doing this from a safe distance.

Nothing much to say here, this move is strictly combo filler, similarly to Ultra Cannon. You're mainly gonna use this move to stall for a cooldown or simply to squeeze in more damage at the end of a combo. You can use this move after Uppercut, any variant of Ultra Spin, and Offloaded Heat Emission. Aside from that, you can use Offloaded Ultra Spin, any variant of Heat Emission, and Puppet Barrage.

This move, unlike [i]Ultra Cannon[/i], is NOT strictly combo filler; it has a surprising amount of value both in combos and in neutral without any of the risks [i]Ultra Cannon[/i] has. It can be used as an area denial tool when used or to force out a block in neutral similarly to [i]Puppet Barrage[/i], which leaves them open for side dash > [i]Boost On[/i] or just pressing [i]Heat Emission[/i]. Singlehandedly THE BEST move to apply [color=#d11010]Uberstacking[/color] (as usual, refer to [color=hsl(39, 100%, 50%)]Techs[/color] and [color=#ff0000]Combos[/color] in [url=https://dogslamloop.com/characters/Puppet_master/index.html]Overviews & Strategy[/url]) by far. You go from doing a mere 7 damage to 14, not including if you use it with [i]Ultra Cannon[/i].

You can evasive bait with this move simply by placing it down and aiming it at them. If they refuse to evasive, you can shoot the cannon or save it for a later combo/attempt to evasive bait again the next time you catch them. If they try to go after the puppet and take their eyes off of you, you can punish them easily assuming you aren't too far away. Do keep in mind that they may be given burst if they hit the puppet before you can hit them.

This move is your main tool for neutral. This move is both unblockable AND uncounterable due to being classified as an explosion move. Although I did say this move is your main tool for neutral, NEVER throw it out randomly without at least wasting their side dash or forcing out a block with one of your other offloaded moves unless you're sure they can't react. It's just barely dodgable with side dash if you throw it out raw. You can use this move before or after any other move during combos, there is no move this cannot combo into, as long as you aren't too close. Your minimum distance to hit this move is side dash range.

You can use this move after M1ing the air two times and follow up with an uppercut as they're falling down, although I only recommend doing this over Heat Emission if you want to follow up with [i]Charged Ultra Cannon[/i]. You can use also use this over [i]Heat Emission[/i] if you cannot get into it's effective range in time. Just like [i]Heat Emission[/i], there is no move this cannot combo into, save for [i]Charged Ultra Cannon[/i] if you refrain from doing the uppercut follow-up mentioned above. You can catch characters during their movement abilities such as Yuji's feints if they're close enough, giving you an opportunity to punish them easily.

Quite frankly, there really isn't much to say about this move. it's almost strictly combo filler; you are NEVER starting a combo with this move unless they're stupid enough to get hit by it during neutral or it drifts behind their block. This move is mainly used to stall for cooldowns during a combo, just like [i]Ultra Cannon[/i]. Although unlike [i]Ultra Cannon[/i], it does a surprisingly high amount of damage. You can do an M1 reset with this move, albeit this requires destruction. I recommend just M1ing the air twice and then hitting the enemy with your 3rd and 4th M1 after they get thrown to avoid blue sparks.

You can use this move outside of it's intended purpose by surfing on it's head after using it. You can stack this move with [i]Heat Emission[/i] to make [i]Heat Emission's[/i] neutral even more annoying. Puppet Master has a variety of techs to learn and apply, most of which are extremely consistent. Many of his techs come from the fact that each move has some way to synergize with each other, which includes even Charged Ultra Cannon. For example, Offloaded Ultra Spin can easily combo into any move while also allowing for completely unevasible damage when used right as the puppet lets go of the target with any move other than Charged Ultra Cannon. Puppet Master general strategy is to use his moves and special to swarm and overload the opponent with pressure in different ways, whether that's to use certain moves to close in for M1s, punishing mistakes, or to keep an opponent at bay with range. If played properly, the opponent is at a disadvantage due to dealing with the threats of both the Puppet Master and the puppets, allowing for easier conversions into comboes. During the start of a game, the first goal is to get around 20-30% of your ultimate bar so you can comfortably start doing the techs Puppet Master has. This can be adjusted higher depending per player.

Use Heat Emission (non use twice) after they've wasted side dash (its both uncounterable and unblockable). Do Offloaded Ultra Spin into front dash after they've wasted side dash if your 4 isn't up or you wanna save it, they're forced to pick which one they wanna block. Both Puppet Barrage and Offloaded Ultra Cannon apply crazy pressure and forces them to block, basically free m1s if they don't track you well enough. Boost On can surprise people during M1 trades if you do M1 > Boost On instead of M1 x2, but don't expect this to work more than once or twice on competent players. Offloaded Ultra Spin is also a very useful interruption tool to punish opponents who don't bother to block it after they evasive or try to attempt their combo on the player.

Honored One's Limitless special can't consistently punish moves like Boost On or a successful Puppet Barrage, which leaves the Gojo with no other options other than to occasionally use their teleport to quickly close the distance against the Puppet Master. On the other hand, the Mechamaru player has a big advantage due to Gojo having subpar mobility, allowing the puppets to have their maximum pressure potential.

Be wary of Gojo's Limitless cooldown during neutral. Use whatever tools you have at your disposal to constantly keep advantage. Stay within your effective range and play how you like to play. For as long as you don't screw up in some certain scenarios, this matchup is an easy win due to the Gojo needing to close the distance.
How should you approach this matchup?

Vessel's quick and agile mobility allows him to quickly close the distance between him and the Puppet Master. While he is an M1 Merchant at his core, it doesn't necessarily constitute that the matchup will be easier, as Mechamaru is at his weakest when forced to M1 trade. Cursed Strikes and Crushing Blow also has i-frames during the move, making Puppet Barrage during M1 trades far less effective. Other than his mobility and i-frames though, he doesn't have anything else that can counter Mechamaru, with his counter being far less effective against the puppets and Heat Emission.

Generally, Yuji's strategy is to use his mobility to quickly close the distance and force M1 trades, so playing passive and going for punishes will be optimal. During neutral, make good use of the offloaded variants of his moves as well as base Heat Emission, as his counter targets the puppet instead of the Mechamaru, or won't trigger on Heat Emission as it is considered to be an "explosion" attack. Fully capitalize out of any hit you can get. Mechamaru's combos are especially effective at getting low HP characters near to death's door in just one encounter. Play smart with your cooldowns, you want to continuously swarm the Yuji with pressure at the right moments (e.g, when they're about to close the distance and intiate an M1 trade).
How should you approach this matchup?

It can stop a base Heat Emission, but at max height it just goes under. Abuse your puppets. Hakari completely lacks the mobility to deal with simultaneous threats, and also lacks the effective range to have any counterplay against a Mechamaru that sits within front dash range. Just play well and cautious, a Hakari genuinely can't do anything if the Mechamaru plays good or for punish.
How should you approach this matchup?

The matchup against Ten Shadows constantly shifts, but it still mostly favors Puppet Master. Don't let that fool you though, Megumi does have a few ways to get some counterplay against Mechamaru. Notably, Divine Dog can track and interrupt Heat Emission if used during startup. Megumi also has good mobility with his R special, which can be used to approach along with Rabbit Escape, or to escape moves like Puppet Barrage. However, Rabbit Escape is less effective against a Mechamaru, simply because it doesn't actually stop the Mechamaru player from using offloaded moves, nor does it restrict his movement (e.g, Heat Emission bypasses Rabbit Escape's restricted movement).

Be cautious over Megumi's R special. A good Megumi will use it to approach you while you have your guard down. Use Heat Emission more conservatively when they have Divine Dog out. Only use it when you are certain they can't react to the startup frame of Heat Emission or escape from it. Ultra Spin, Heat Emission, and all offloaded variants can all be used during Rabbit Escape. At best, you can convert, at worst the Megumi doesn't get their combo. Play a bit more safely, reckless skill usage will get you punished one way or another.

A majority of neutral counterplay against Puppet Master is to save your dashes to retreat from any unfavorable scenario the player finds themselves in. There are a total of three to four moves that a Puppet Master has that they can use in neutral, depending on their playstyle. Do note that a skilled [noauto]Puppet Master[/noauto] will use a combination of their neutral tools to overwhelm your defenses, so the key points in shutting down his neutral is to [color=hsl(217, 91%, 60%)]keep calm, read, and adapt to the situation accordingly.[/color] [u][i]Puppet Barrage[/i] (RR)[/u] is a pressure tool used to force the player to either block, retreat, or use a move with lingering i-frames. Retreating by moving away from the Puppet Master and then blocking once the puppets dash if they're at range. This saves a dash that can be used to retreat against other moves, or to gain an advantage if the [noauto]Puppet Master[/noauto] goes for an M1 trade. Alternatively, certain characters can use their mobility or AoE moves here to also deal with the puppets, though this is extremely niche and might lead to the opposing player getting punished if the move puts them in a noticeable amount of stun time. [u][i]Offloaded Ultra Spin[/i] (R1)[/u] is a neutral tool most often used at the midrange when the puppet can spawn behind the opponent, forcing the opposing player to block the puppet and leave their back exposed. At close range, the opposing player can side dash out of the R1's path safely. Alternatively, if both players are at mid range, then your options start to differ: if they leave Heat Emission's effective range, then side dash away. If not, block the R1 and react to whatever follow-up they go for afterwards. [u][i]Heat Emission[/i] (4)[/u] is the strongest move Puppet Master has in neutral. It's a midrange rush move with a big AoE explosion at the front that CANNOT be blocked or countered on base, and is usually the straw the breaks the camel's back if side dash is on cooldown. Stay out of it's effective range as much as possible. If you are within range and the Puppet Master uses it, use your side dash to retreat.

At the start of the round, using pokes is very important to determine how his opponent prefers to play their character. Most characters can be broken down into aggressive and passive optimal playstyles. For example, Naoya and Yuji are optimal when played aggressive, and they prefer close range engagement, while Ryu and Hanami are passive, and prefer to stay further away from conflict. Register’s goal is to understand how their kits are optimally played, and prevent his opponent from making moves that get them into their optimal situation.

You have to factor in two things when encountering an opponent The preferred playstyle of their character The choices they make to enforce their preferred playstyle The most important factor is the preferred playstyle of their character. You will punish the wrong choices they make to enforce it (i.e. a bad front dash) and prevent the “correct” choices from punishing you. Most playstyles can be broken under two categories: Rushdown and Zoner. The definitions should not be taken too literally, but most characters operate better depending on their range from their opponent. Reggie is the cog in this, as he can be either Rushdown or Zoner. Here is how you should play against these playstyles:

Characters who you should look out for are: Yuji, Naoya, and Todo Since your opponent will always want to approach you, you must counter that. Your most important moves are Gushing Wound, Garage Sale, and Littering. You must use these to keep range. Gushing Wound should always be thrown out in further engagements (when there is more of a distance between you and the opponent) to slow down their approach. Garage Sale does a similar job to Gushing Wound in keeping them out, but can be used in closer engagements to push them away. Littering should be used in a fashion similar to Choso’s Blood Orb that is left behind by Aerial Flowing Red Scale, giving yourself an area where you are immune from combos (you can activate Littering while stunned).

Characters you should look out for are: Ryu, Hanami, and Haruta. Since your opponent wants to stay as far away from you as possible, you must use your pokes and range closing tools to counter that. The most important ones are Gushing Wound, Garage Sale, and Red Seal Speed Crash. These options will slow down their means of running, Gushing Wound stuns them for a bit when hit (they won’t typically be blocking since they’re running), Garage Sale stuns them, and Speed Crash (especially Red Seal) is great at closing the gap fast. These are all suggestions, and oftentimes in gameplay, you do not need to follow these ideas, but they are generally the standard answers for these playstyles.

Gushing Wound is part of Register's initial starting kit. This allows for the quick use of a poke, and if landed, chips down the opponent by 12. The move is unblockable, and if not blocked, it serves as a great interruption tool for further range opponents. The move itself has a range of ~200 studs, and has the perk of being fast, which is great for stopping Ryu from clearing his resource easily or halting runners. This move can catch many off guard with its small windup, fast speed, and range, and is generally very safe to use freely.

[color=hsl(3, 93%, 63%)]Red Seal Gushing Wound[/color] acts as a shotgun that deals ~20 damage. Register can use it as a follow up to M1s or after a side dash to the opponent. Do not use it from further away, it is meant to deal immediate damage.

Blunt Trauma is a powerful move in Register's kit. It serves as a punishing option after ragdoll, but one should keep in mind that whiffing the move is very punishable. The effect provided by the move makes it easy to follow up and harder to punish, since once hit, they cannot side dash and are susceptible to further attack. One must absolutely not use this outside of extending in combos, since the blockable natural of it makes it easy to counter. The usual reaction to this is to front dash away, so using Garage Sale as a follow-up is nice. Red Seal Blunt Trauma is very hard hitting, and it extends the debuff effect, however, it is the most evasive punishable move in Register's kit, since it leaves him out in the animation.

Restless Gambler is a scrappy brawler with tools intended to be able to used in almost any situation, which is meant to make him very well-rounded. However, as a result of little to no movement options and a lack of ranged options (outside of Reserve Balls), he ends up being a brawler who rarely gets an opening, making it so that every opportunity he gets must be capitalized on heavily. Restless Gambler gameplay mainly focuses around his second ability, Shutter Doors, as it provides combo extension, move variants, aerial mobility and can create a threat through the use of aerial Rough Energy. His neutral and disadvantage states are terrible due to his lack of good get-off-me tools and pokes, leading him to mainly rely on M1 trades to get much of anything done.

Honored One generally M1 trades better and can invalidate your counter with Reversal Red and intentionally missing his moves. You can counter Rapid Punches after 1R but it can just as easily be baited out for more damage. Honored One Limitless can also catch you out of the air after jumping on shutter doors or during aerial 3, making these options significantly less viable in this matchup.

Use your counter to invalidate any wake-up shenanigans a Honored One player may try with 3. 1+2 can punish Lapse Blue on block and should be one of your main tools in this matchup. Keep the fight grounded, Honored One won't mind you going into the air to use Limitless on you to then lead into a 50/50 with 3.
What should you do versus them?

Restless Gambler generally outclasses Vessel in close combat altercations. Restless Gambler counter is a decent tool in this matchup as Vessel moves are very telegraphed, though he can feint. Although Vessel also has a lower HP pool than Restless Gambler, with some simple combos doing a majority of his HP. Fever Crush, as an example, would do 1/4th of a Vessel's health bar.

Be wary of Vessel's feints. A simple feint can put you into a bad spot, especially after a counter. Manji Kick can counter your Reserve Balls. Avoid trying to combo start with 1+2 as much in this matchup. You can attempt to bait out a Manji Kick by using Reserve Ball and then turning to a slightly different direction.
What should you do versus them?
A ditto is a ditto. Not much else to say here. The most notable thing in this matchup is that you can use aerial 3 to counter their aerial 3.

Salaryman is an intricate and technical character, specializing in burst damage and interrupting the opponent's attacks with timing. Performed accurately enough, Salaryman can inflict temporary debuffs to the enemy that make defending against your onslaught increasingly difficult. Neutral tools such as Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut keep your opponent on edge while you prepare your Ratio Point in order to break through their defenses. Salaryman offers unique combo routing that allows for powerful offense, regardless of if the opponent is stunned or not.

Salaryman works best either close or medium range from the enemy. Ensuring that a Ratio Point is always applied and that you get the maximum value out of the Ratio Point possible (Ratio Point variants, interruption staggers, etc.) will allow you to overwhelm and destroy your enemies in only a few interactions.

Salaryman's skills can be split into two sections: Close-range optimal and medium-range optimal. If you seek to use these moves in neutral, maintaining distance and timing will net you the best value. Also, you are in a much superior position when the enemy has a staggered limb, so aim to achieve that as soon as possible. Cleaving Whirlwind causes Salaryman to lunge a notable distance, so it can be used as a gap-closer from afar, followed up by a mix-up if you spin around the enemy to hit them behind their block. You can also punish enemies that use their own attacks too haphazardly by hitting them with the Ratio Point variant, interrupting and staggering their limb. Severance Kick gets most of its value in M1 trading. When you are blocking an enemy's onslaught of punches, weaving in Reverse Kick will stun the enemy long enough for you to punish them. Also, if most of your moves are all on cooldown but you have the enemy in an M1 chain, you can kick them away to gain enough distance to recover. Blunt Cut is punishable on block without Ratio Point, so avoid using it at all in neutral without it. If you hit an enemy with a Ratio Point, try to dash into them fast enough to convert off of it into more damage. Cross Cut is a consistent way, if you're fast enough, to get through a blocking opponent using the second half of the attack, which is unblockable no matter what. Finally, Stabilize, when used at the perfect distance, can stun opponents using attacks poorly without needing to use your Ratio Point. You can also try to use Stabilize in an M1 trade as you would with Reverse Kick to get the enemy off of you and give you a moment to prepare a Ratio Point.

This is expanded upon greatly in the Combos page, but there are still some details to know before bringing Salaryman into ranked matches: Severance Kick can be cancelled into Blunt Cut if the enemy does not block the kick. This is especially powerful with a Ratio Point applied Stabilize can be cancelled into both Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut with or without a Ratio Point so that you can keep up the pressure Making combos slower and more methodical can make it more likely for your enemy to try blocking or counter-attacking, which is when you should strike back with a Ratio Point variant, resetting the cooldown and giving you far more damage

Enemies very often use their evasive after being hit with Severance Kick, so try to condition them to use it by starting interactions with it. If they choose not to use it, you can instead cancel into Blunt Cut as mentioned before. There is a surprising amount of time you have to cancel into Blunt Cut, so once you're sure that they won't use their evasive, take initiative. Also, ragdolling your opponent in any way and then applying a Ratio Point (since they can see when you activate it) will pressure them to move before you convert into big damage with a well-timed Stabilize or Cleaving Whirlwind.

[i] one optimal route is: ratioed stabilise bypassing a block -> fully charged blunt cut -> cleaving whirlwind + Ratio -> wake up reverse kick [/I]

Nanami's greatest weakness are enemy's counter skills, making him even harder to play. When facing a counter character he needs to bet if they are going for their counter when they face a untrue combo / a neutral move OR if they want to keep it as mental pressure, making the Nanami waver, not commiting to untrue routes just because they have a counter ready. To deal with a counter character Nanami needs to learn counter bait Example: 3 m1s -> stabilise -> whiff cleaving whirlwind If they counter you get a combo. If they don't you don't get punished for it. Make sure you miss cleaving whirlwind not right on their face, as the lingering hitbox could indirectly land To put it more simply. Nanami has to do even more to work around their counter.

[b] Post 1.78 update [/b] nanami gets to convert into full combos after bypassing a block/interrupting with ratioed cleaving whirlwind, blunt cut, stabilise. However he doesn't get conversion if he doesn't interrupt with blunt cut. He does get to convert with the following route: (if the opponent doesnt have evasive even if nanami doenst interrupt) Ratio imbued Cleaving Whirlwind -> Cross cut -> backdash -> reverse kick

The ratio Technique is tied to the R special button, also known as [b] Ratio Point [/b]. When pressed it starts a quick time event going over the target's head, visible to the Salaryman only. However the opposing player can figure out if it was activated by a distinct eye flash vfx, but he won't be aware if Salaryman succeeded in the QTE. The Ratio Point QTE is a bar positioned above the target's head. A circle slides on the bar and R has to be pressed again when the circle overlaps the red 7:3 line, if performed successfully, the opponent will be marked for the next 4.5 seconds, the timer will be displayed in the R special bar, going from empty to full for those 4.5 seconds. Ratio can be used in any stun, endlag, ragdoll The circle slides faster the lower the hp of the target is. Ratio Point also makes the attacks it affects deal more damage. Ratio Point allows Cleaving Whirlwind and Blunt Cut to get interruption properties. [b] POST UPDATE 1.78 [/b]: Ratio Point gets its Cooldown refreshed on interruption/hitting block with 1, 3, 4 skills Stabilise when imbued with ratio is now considered a strong block hitter due to its sheer speed

When ratio is successfully landed, some of Salaryman skills gain extra attributes. Which are: Cleaving Whirlwind bypasses block Severance Kick and reverse kick aren't affected Blunt Cut bypasses block Cross Cut (aerial blunt cut) hits block if Ratio Point is done on the first hit and it launches upwards if it's done on the second hit, the second hit bypasses block regardless. Stabilise hits block and stuns for longer (Stagger will be mentioned at interruptions) Uppercut does +4 damage and it ragdols further, extending to Cleaving Whirlwind (consistent) or fully charged Blunt Cut (inconsistent) 4th M1 does +4 damage and it ragdols further.

By using Salaryman's fourth M1 on someone who has a Ratio Point on them, the M1 will deal double the damage, totaling to 8 (10 in Overtime), as well as knocking the enemy substantially farther back. In Overtime, this M1 becomes unblockable.

By using Salaryman's uppercut on someone who has a Ratio Point on them, the upperut will deal double the damage, totaling to 8 (10 in Overtime), as well as knocking the enemy substantially farther up in the air, allowing you to hit the enemy with Cleaving Whirlwind if aimed properly during their descent. In Overtime, this uppercut becomes unblockable.

When Salaryman is in Overtime, having a Ratio Point on the opponent allows your downslam to also have a Black Flash variant, like how your fourth M1 and uppercut normally do, dealing twice the damage as a regular downslam, totaling to 10.

A lunging strike that is blockable from the front, accompanied with melee i-frames to make it easier to get in someone's face. Salaryman arms his cleaver and spins forward, slashing downward and dealing 12 damage upon connection, pushing the enemy back and ragdolling them. It has a 16-second cooldown.

Cleaving Whirlwind is a consistent neutral pressure tool. You can attempt to spin your character behind the opponent's block if they anticipate it to knock them down. With 46 frames of startup, it is certainly reactable, but you can definitely play mind games.

Cleaving Whirlwind can be seamlessly cancelled into if Salaryman uses the attack right after successfully hitting Stabilize. If it is the Stabilize Ratio Point variant, you can guarantee a strike with Cleaving Whirlwind, since the enemy is unable to block.

As mentioned above, Salaryman has melee i-frames throughout the startup and active frames. This allows you to avoid people's attempts to cancel your strike with an M1, barrage attack (Like Locust Guy's Clever) or grab attack (Like Cursed Partner's Second Wind).

Like the normal version of Cleaving Whirlwind, Salaryman lunges forward, spinning and striking the opponent. With a ratio point applied to the target, the strike deals an additional 4 damage, totaling to 16 damage. If the attack either hits a blocking enemy or interrupts the enemy, their right arm will be staggered. This shrinks their blocking angle substantially for 7 seconds. It will also immediately reset your special's cooldown.

A quick forward kick delivered by Salaryman that pushes enemies forward a slight distance. The kick itself deals 12 damage. However, it has the unique property of being able to launch throwables at high speeds, similar to Vessel's special. This kicked throwable deals 15 damage. Lastly, if the enemy does not use their evasive, blunt cut can be seamlessly cancelled into after the kick connects. The kick does not remove the Ratio Point from the enemy.

By holding backwards and using Severance Kick, Salaryman will instead perform Reverse Kick. This deals exactly the same damage as the normal severance kick, with the added bonus of both being unblockable and stunning enemies upon interruption (similar to Vessel's Divergent Fist, but not on block). By utilizing this variant during an M1 trade, you can very easily interrupt the enemy's M1, stunning them and guaranteeing yourself plenty of damage. Do note that, unlike the default kick, Reverse Kick can not be cancelled into Blunt Cut.

Salaryman enters a stance, charging a quick swing, then stepping forward almost instantly, damaging those in his path. Blunt Cut can be charged for a moment for an added 5 damage, totaling to 14 damage dealt upon contact. Blunt Cut can also be seamlessly cancelled into following a successful Severance Kick.

When Ratio Point is applied to a target, using Blunt Cut through them will make the attack unblockable, as well as dealing an additional 4 damage, up to a maximum of 18 damage if fully charged. If the attack either hits a blocking enemy or interrupts the enemy, their left leg will be staggered. This makes the enemy completely unable to dash for 7 seconds. It will also immediately reset your special's cooldown.

If airborne when using Blunt Cut, Salaryman will instead glide down, slamming the ground and anyone directly beneath him. This first slam is blockable, otherwise dealing 5 damage. If the initial slam hits an enemy, regardless of if they are blocking or not, a second strike will automatically be used, this time being unblockable, dealing 4 damage, and sending the enemy tumbling back (though they will remain standing). As a side note, if the first slam is hit on a ragdolled opponent, they will be unable to use their ragdoll cancel so that the second hit can connect.

The Ratio Point variant of Cross Cut innately has two sub-variants depending on when the Ratio Point is applied onto the enemy. If the first slam connects whilst the enemy has a Ratio Point applied, the slam will deal an additional 6 damage and making the slam unblockable. If the slam interrupts or hits an opponent's block, it will stagger their left leg (see Blunt Cut: Ratio Point), as well as resetting your special's cooldown. If the Ratio Point is not applied until right before the second slash of the attack hits, it will instead amplify the latter half of the attack, increasing the slice's damage by 6, throwing the enemy upwards and ragdolled. If the slice interrupts or hits an opponent's block, it will stagger their right arm (see Cleaving Whirlwind: Ratio Point), as well as resetting your special's cooldown. The angle of the second Ratio Point variant allows Cleaving Whirlwind to be smoothly hit while the enemy is falling back down, if aimed correctly. Theoretically, though very difficult and situational, both ratio strikes can be hit in a single Cross Cut if the enemy is interrupted with the first ratio slam (resetting your special cooldown), and you re-apply a ratio on the enemy before the second slice connects. This will deal a total of 21 damage.

Salaryman reels their arm back and thrusts their cleaver forward, crushing the opponent's stomach, dealing 6 damage and pushing the enemy back. If Stabilize interrupts an opponent's attack, it will do a prolonged stagger where the enemy clutches their stomach longer, and Salaryman twirls his cleaver. This is a great time to apply a Ratio Point, as the enemy will be stunned long enough for it to be done safely. Additionally, after Stabilize connects, the endlag can be cut short by using either Cleaving Whirlwind or Blunt Cut immediately after.

If the enemy is hit with Stabilize while a ratio is applied to them, the aforementioned interruption stagger will trigger regardless of if the enemy was interrupted or not, dealing the same 6 damage. If the opponent is interrupted, it will deal a total of 10 damage, as well as resetting your special cooldown. It should be noted that, while Stabilize can hit ragdolled opponents, the ratio variant will not be used and the ratio itself will not be removed from the target.

Using your special places a 7:3 ratio on your opponents head for a moment. Pressing special again when the circle is on top of the red line locks it in place for 5 seconds. If you miss this timing, your special will be put on cooldown. This Ratio Point is the cornerstone of Salaryman's entire kit, granting him access to different properties to his M1s, as well as new variants for many of his moves. Hitting a Ratio Point variant with certain moves under certain conditions will stagger either the opponent's right arm or left leg. A staggered right arm drastically shortens the opponent's blocking angle for 7 seconds, and a staggered left leg makes the opponent unable to dash for 7 seconds. Interrupting an opponent with a Ratio Point variant will reset your special cooldown. In Overtime, there is no cooldown for your special. Base kit skills enhanced with Ratio Point: Fourth M1 Uppercut Cleaving Whirlwind Blunt Cut Cross Cut Stabilize Awakening skills enhanced with Ratio Point: Downslam Ratio Breaker I Ratio Breaker II Ratio Breaker III Ratio Breaker IV Sharpen Erosion Interrogate I Interrogate II Collapse I

Also his evasive bait is better and more safe than Salaryman's)

Sky Assassin is an Aerial-focused glass-cannon. While strong in her own right, she has access to a 15 second long "install" that empowers her moveset making her a much larger threat that charges much faster than your usual awakening. Sky Assassin's rather short cooldowns, alongside her ability to fully reset said cooldowns with her install, allow her to dish out major damage in a very short amount of time.

Blind Rage's hitbox is pretty small, and with the newest update (as of typing this) getting rid of its ability to pick up ragdolled opponents, Blind Rage is best used [b]IN, AND ONLY IN[/b][u][/u] a m1 chain. If Sky Assassin wants to be stylish, and thinks she can time the grab after their uppercut (Blind Rage has the same properties of every other melee move, where it's possible to time the hitbox to land on ragdolled opponents while they're a certain height in the air), it is landable! She just needs to be mindful of their evasive meter. Due to Sky Assassin's aerial focus, she should prioritize flying horizontally, crashing into the ground until she lands three hits, which at that point she should fly vertically If Sky Assassin's opponent evasives out of the grab, it will cause an automatic punishment on Sky Assassin, resulting in her being true-ragdolled for 5 full seconds. This punish is blockable by Sky Assassin, if she is not currently in her air m1, or if the air m1 was not missed via evasive..
Blind Rage (temper variant) has two powerful swings before the grab, both are blockable and the move to be punished on-reaction in the event of missing one of the two swings.

Sky Distortion is a pretty simple move. Sky Assassin does a small twirl, grabbing the sky and hitting her opponents with it. If used in the air, it does a small lunge forward! If looking at your opponent while in the air and using it, it'll launch her horizontally towards her opponent, blocking or not. Do note that this does NOT hit ragdoll, but can be timed while the opponent is in the air. An inconsistent move it can combo into is the jump variant of Turbulence, as timing it can extend the time the opponent is in the air (Stalling her own cooldowns, or leading into a few extra hits with Thin Ice Breaker). If she's in Sky Veil, she can try to catch her opponent off guard by using the aerial version of Sky Distortion, giving Sky Assassin mobility towards her opponent, in case of a blunder from them (Front dash away, move to predict where she, etc.)

Unlike its normal variant, temper Sky Distortion turns into a ranged blockbreaker! Using it while on the ground picks up debris, and adds an additional 5 damage because the debris is being picked up. When the hit lands on the opponent, they will flung flung TOWARDS the opposite direction the move hit them from, launching them closer to Sky Assassin If temper Sky Distortion hits someone when using it in the air (who is not ragdolled), will throw them up into the air instead, allowing to chain all four of your air m1s from the boost temper gives Sky Assassin, since it launches the opponent high enough to initiate the command. If Sky Assassin's opponent is ragdolled and [b][u]IN THE SKY[/u][/b], they can use temper Sky Distortion to make the move become an auto-targeting bullet that will, unless the opponent uses evasive, hit the enemy no matter the direction Sky Assassin is facing. The only thing that stops the bullet is a wall. When the bullet lands, it performs the same mechanics as what the normal variant does, launching the opponent towards Sky Assassin. If used properly, can lead to another set of air m1s on the opponent.

Sky Veil is a straight forward skill. Sky Assassin shrouds herself via Sky Manipulation, and goes invisible to the naked eye. She moves around with increased speed for 2 seconds, and pressing any keybind set to a move allows her to use that move while invisible, unshrouding herself and using the move simultaneously. while she is invisible, she cannot m1 or dash (any direction), and is limited to walking with increased speed. She is able to jump. If the 2 seconds run out, or if R is clicked again, Sky Assassin will unveil herself, and don't be able to use moves for a VERY small duration.

Sky Assassin's combos might be considered "low damage" in her base kit because of how many Blue Sparks her combos add. Although she may cause their opponent to gain evasive quickly, this factor does NOT take away any of the Megumi (potential) she has. Be smart, and combo wisely!

Sky Assassin's Aerial M1 has [b]no required[/b] action needed in order to trigger it, allowing her to punish targets who use certain movement tools, such as high wall jumps or Restless Gambler's Shutter Door bounce. Sky Assassin using her superior air mobility to punish Restless Gambler. UroRender:PIPTA
After doing 3 M1s and then an uppercut surf on her opponent, using aerial Sky Distortion will allow Sky Assassin to do the aimable version of Thin Ice Breaker which allows her to get an air M1 in.

After using Blind Rage and aiming her camera up in the last few seconds of flight, Sky Assassin can cause the enemy to be flung upwards into her, where she can then M1 into an air M1 before side dashing directly after for a third air M1.

If Sky Veil is used on a move that is currently on cooldown, it will do version where she has no exit lag, which allows her to sneak up on your opponent for a unreactable m1 (Leave them guessing where she could be with some mind games).

When using grounded Turbulence, aiming backwards then shiftlocking forwards will make the hit box reappear in front of her without visuals too the enemy. (Do know it is still blockable and Sky Assassin can't hit around block with it)

Honored One is the "average", not really failing in any categories while not excelling in any either, but against Sky Assassin, that changes. Honored One can easily counter Sky Assassin's moves by being able to teleport. Surprisingly, this counters most of Sky Assassin's moves. Turbulence? Teleport. Thin Ice Breaker whiff? Teleport (then again, Sky Assassin shouldn't be using Thin Ice Breaker in neutral anyways). Sky Assassin has less time to catch Honored One off guard with Sky Veil because of Honored One's first m1 being slightly faster (if predicted), which does slightly hinder Sky Assassin if she's trying to use Dark Mango Psychology (Please check [url=https://dogslamloop.com/characters/Sky_assassin/index.html#sec-dark-mango-psychology]here[multicolor=#ef4444,#3b82f6][/multicolor][/url] to know what is being said) to get a few quick m1s in. If there is one thing Honored One does the best, it's m1 trading. What truly makes Sky Veil risky to use would be Honored One's 2+R variant, where using it during an opponent's move freezes them in place. Since Sky Veil lasts a whopping two seconds, Honored One has ≤ 2 seconds to simply click two buttons to interrupt Sky Assassin.

Vessel is more annoying than he is difficult to deal with. Vessel doesn't leap high enough when using their feints for mobility, so Sky Assassin can't punish them. Even if she tries to catch them off guard with Turbulence, Vessel gets just high enough to leap over the move, rendering it useless in neutral. Vessel's m1s are faster, so m1 trading with Vessel is rigged in their favor, unless they fail to read a side dash. Punishing Vessel isn't really an option, and Sky Assassin has better odds by just focusing on combos after a successful m1 trade instead. When m1 trading — or when an opponent uses any move in general — Manji Kick is Vessel's best friend! This is especially the case for Sky Assassin as most of Sky Assassin's moves are parryable. The only move that isn't parryable is Turbulence, plus all of its variants (the jump variant of Turbulence is semi-parryable, as its damage changes from melee to explosion). Sky Assassin's best bet would be to try and predict when Vessel will strike, and bait out their Manji Kick, as that's all they really have going for them.

The one thing that makes Sky Assassin powerful against her opponents is the ability to throw back projectiles and shut down any aerial advances. Restless Gambler is a prime example of this! If Restless Gambler wants an unblockable variant to their aerial Rough Energy, they have to use Shutter Doors in order to reach enough height in the air. Luckily for Sky Assassin, it simply doesn't matter whether or not Restless Gambler bounces on Shutter Doors! If they do bounce, Sky Assassin can hold down their M1s and instantly shut down the move, leading to [b][u]TWO[/u][/b] of their moves being on cooldown, while Sky Assassin didn't have to waste anything in order to land a hit! This is because like some of the other character's moves, Sky Assassin's M1s focus on distance from ground! so by Restless Gambler using Shutter Doors, they doom themselves into wasting one to two moves! Shutter Door plus Reserve Balls is always a good combo starter when it comes to Restless Gambler, but Sky Assassin can take that for themselves! Sky Distortion reflects any projectiles and hits the opponent with them! Even some bigger entities, like Open and Hollow Purple, can get reflected! Although they will most likely kill Sky Assassin in the process. This mechanic allows Sky Assassin to reflect the variant, causing Restless Gambler if caught off guard, to be hit by their own move! The only real threats are if Sky Assassin wastes evasive early, since Restless Gambler's parry will be used to maximize damage, as Sky Assassin shut down most of their moves. If Sky Assassin thinks Restless Gambler is going to parry, she can use the jump variant of Turbulence without hitting the initial kick so that the parry has time to go away, so she can punish Restless Gambler.

If Sky Assassin gets hit down because of evasive being used in the sky (AKA Sky Assassin whiffing the punch and being set with major endlag, causing the punch to land instead of being blocked), it'll knock Sky Assassin down into a move. This doesn't seem like a problem at first, but keep in mind that Ten Shadows is able to hit ragdoll with every move, meaning Sky Assassin's blunder can cause her to be caught in a combo from Ten Shadows, or at the LEAST an m1 chain after Ten Shadows uses Toad. Ten Shadows is good at zoning Sky Assassin, but can also cancel Sky Assassin out of any move with their [u][b]TOAD[/b][/u]. Toad can pick Sky Assassin up for an easy m1 chain. Every move is punishable by toad if Sky Assassin whiffs; [i]EVERY MOVE.[/i] If Sky Assassin uses temper, Ten Shadows can use Toad. If Sky Assassin manages to get temper off, any move can also be cancelled if used in neutral. [i]Sky Assassin has to rely on combos in order to win.[/i] If she is even caught using a move in neutral, Toad will punish Sky Assassin. Along with having to combo, if Ten Shadows evasives in the middle of Sky Assassin's combo, since she doesn't have any moves that have true ragdoll, Ten Shadows can punish Sky Assassin. Sky Assassin relies on precise and high damage combos in a short amount of time, and anything that kills that flow during the combo can put an end to Sky Assassin.

Sky Assassin's worst enemy is [color=#fff8f8]Rika[/color] when fighting Cursed Partners, as Sky Veil is obsolete if [color=#fff8f8]Rika[/color]'s moves are back. Turbulence's ground variant in Sky Veil does [b][i]NOT[/i][/b] counter any [color=#fff8f8]Rika[/color] moves, so Sky Assassin's best option is to either not use Sky Veil at all, or wait until Rika's moves are used. Cursed Partners can keep Sky Assassin at a distance while dishing out constant damage from combos that will chip down Sky Assassin's health FAST. If Sky Assassin can close the distance between her and the Cursed Partners, she might be able to put in some good damage against the Cursed Partners. Sky Assassin should take advantage of if Cursed Partners uses Outburst, as she doesn't want Cursed Partners to capitalize off of a blunder from her two blockable moves that have a lot of endlag on whiff/block. [i][b] SKY ASSASSIN NEEDS TO BE SURE TO PREDICT EVASIVE AFTER BLIND RAGE[/b][/i], as Cursed Partners can easily capitalize off of ragdolled opponents.
"You Fujiwara are always in my way! Are you that afraid of me becoming somebody?!"

Sky Assassin's going to wish that her moves weren't close ranged when she's done fighting Disaster Plants! considering every move has long endlag if whiffed, or is blockable if far ranged, she's about as strong as a Gazelle is when fighting a Lion. What's that? Gazelles don't fight Lions, they run? That's exactly Sky Assassin's plan! This is one of the only times that the close range character [b][u]CANNOT[/u][/b] play aggressively. Sky Assassin NEEDS to play passively, so her best bets are to: Pray Disaster Plants messes up Surging Thorns in neutral, so she can immediately use Blind Rage Pray Disaster Plants gets distracted while using their R variants, so she can immediately use Blind Rage Pray Disaster Plants isn't in a flower field, so she can immediately use Blind Rage Pray Disaster Plants gets hit enough to let her temper meter get high, so she can immediately use temper Blind Rage The whole match relies on the only semi-reliable blockbreaker, Blind Rage. Blind Rage, since applying pressure with any other move will get Sky Assassin stuck in a combo, helps her damage Disaster Plants! This damage can eventually (with a LOT of time) build up enough meter to use temper, which will let Sky Assassin finally have an unblockable move that can hit Disaster Plants without being [i]as[/i] at risk of being full comboed! ...hopefully.

Granite blast or Appetizer?: Jump variant of Sky Distortion ([kbd]2[/kbd]) to close the gap while dealing extra damage! Holding Granite Blast?: Use Turbulence ([kbd]3[/kbd]) to cancel the move while launching True Cannon towards her! True Cannon names a move, and Sky Assassin will have a solution! With the help of their amazing "I hate True Cannon" kit, True Cannon becomes a near non-lethal threat for once! To counter his melee attacks like Second Helping and Unsatisfied, Sky Assassin [i]could[/i] use Sky Veil ([kbd]R[/kbd]) and instantly use Turbulence for the parry variant, but the most optimal route would be to simply avoid them, and then counter attack with the ground version of Turbulence if she try to gain distance. If Sky Assassin wants to be stylish, she can use the jump variant of Turbulence to hover above a Granite Blast from True Cannon to get an easy hit, which will be easier if the True Cannon is panicking.

This is one of the only matchups that is really equal for Sky Assassin. Both Lucky Coward and Sky Assassin have to be careful in this match! If Sky Assassin is dodged, Lucky Coward can use the endlag to get a few moves off on Sky Assassin, plus a miracle. On the opposite end, if Lucky Coward wastes evasive, Sky Assassin can get them to red, and sometimes even get rid of a bar of miracles! In the end, it all boils down to who is going to play more aggressively, and who will capitalize off of a blunder. Both characters are able to deal with each other relatively easy.

No matter what Sky Assassin presses, Black Death will always have the upper hand. Anything Sky Assassin does can and WILL get countered, even if it's unintentional. Sky Veil, just like Sky Assassin's matchup with Cursed Partners, is also rendered useless. If Black Death uses Earthen Insect Trance ([kbd]R[/kbd]) right before Sky Assassin uses Sky Veil, Black Death will constantly know where she is. That, along with the short stun it gives, that can cancel heavy moves like Blind Rage, and allow Black Death to get the upper hand on Sky Assassin. If Black Death does not use Earthen Insect Trance, Injuries apply a faint glow each tick it hits, allowing for further shutdown of Sky Veil. Beyond Sky Veil, Black Death also can outrange Sky Assassin. Yes, detach is parryable via Sky Distortion, but Festering Strikes makes most close range moves useless, as it naturally parries, and Black Death's kit is already strong on its own, so thinks such as Sky Distortion and Thin Ice Breaker get flung off without any real punishment to Black death. Overall, the matchup will NOT go well.

Pretty self explanatory, the [color=hsl(0, 100%, 80%)]Sky Assassins[/color] will be in a fight that'll have more time in the air than on the ground. The match will be based on who has better knowledge of both Jujutsu Shenanigans and Sky Assassin.

Star Rage is an M1 Merchant reliant on true and safe combos due to having no evasive bait. She has extremely moderate neutral control with [i]Garuda Stab Variant[/i] being on a 20s cooldown and only one safe follow-up, that being [i]Garuda Rebound[/i]. Star Rage can dish out extremely high damage combos when their opponents use their evasive, and can still be fully viable if her opponent never uses their evasive. Star Rage is known for extremely high damage, "techy" combos that require a higher level of mechanical skill and game sense than other characters. Most of her moves do not hit on grounded ragdoll, making using her moves on getup a common playstyle. Her safe/true ragdoll combos require difficult timings, and combining this with her high endlag on her skills makes mistiming and other mistakes extremely critical and guarantees you to be punished by your opponent. When Star Rage is played appropriately to her full potential, she is extremely deadly and will outclass other M1 Merchant archetypes.

Star Rage has little to no consistent way to bait evasive - a majority of her moves lack the pressure to choke out an evasive as other moves would. For instance, Garuda Stab's R variant struggles to bait evasive as it doesn't have many high damage, threatening, and safe conversions. Garuda Stab R into Garuda Rebound is the safest guaranteed conversion off of Garuda Stab R Garuda Stab R into Rising Rage on getup requires excellent timing and is evasive punishable if expected Garuda Stab R in Mass Breaker can be easily reacted to and punished with evasive
Keep your distance after Garuda Stab R to make sure you can't be evasive punished. M1 M1 M1 GARUDA STAB (R) GARUDA REBOUND FIRST USE GARUDA REBOUND SECOND USE

Star Rage's Neutral is dependent on Garuda Stab R to engage without an m1 trade, and rarely mass breaker to finish someone off if they waste side dash. When Garuda Stab R is on cooldown, Star Rage will be left with just M1s to engage. Garuda Stab R Variant heavily carries Star Rage's neutral game in her kit - it has extremely long range, does 21 damage, and is unblockable. It also has low endlag, and places her safely in the air where she cannot be punished. It is an amazing way to engage and also her only viable option in neutral. Garuda Rebound's second use can allow the Star Rage to engage safely, as the second use cancels Front Dashes, M1s and blocking. If the opponent tries to Block the Front Dash or Side Dash M1, they won't be able to parry the secound use of Garuda Rebound, letting the Star Rage do chip damage. If the Star Rage manages to hit the Front Dash they can simply aim Garuda Rebound away and continue using M1s. The only viable strategy for the opponent is to back off and avoid getting hit by Garuda Rebound's second use. Mass Breaker in neutral can only be viable if her opponent wastes their sidedash, as the long windup and endlag allows them to easily react and punish. This is only good for chip damage, and is more optimal to be saved for combos. Garuda Rebound is extremely reactable and the parry window is very lenient. When Star Rage tries to parry back, often she is too close and still in endlag from the second use, or the parry will pass through her and not go back to her opponent. Parrying is very inconsistent and also has no safe conversions. Base Garuda Stab can act similarly to Honored One's Rapid Punches in M1 trades as it is an unblockable grab and can grab from longer range than M1s.

Star Rage's tech is essential for dealing high damage safe combos, true combos, and 90+ damage combos on opponents who waste their evasive. Her combos and tech are flashy, risky, and require practice to pull off. TECH GUIDE IMPORTANCE [i]Landing Skill on Getup[/i] Star Rage uses skill and hits her opponent the moment they stand up from ragdoll. If timed correctly, it is completely red and uncounterable. Allows her to extend her combo off ragdoll with moves that don't hit grounded ragdoll. [i]True Aerial Mass Breaker[/i] Star Rage does a short pause before her 3rd M1 to jump, and hits her opponent with her 3rd m1 in the air. Mass Breaker is immediately used while looking down, and the opponent is ragdolled in front of her for getup combo extension. Allows Star Rage to combo extend with Rising Rage for a risky high damage true combo, or a safe combo with Garuda Stab R. [i]Garuda Rebound Cooldown Cancel[/i] If Star Rage is still in animation or endlag of Rising Rage or Mass Breaker when Garuda Rebound First Use returns to her, the cooldown will be refunded even if the move hit the opponent. Allows Star Rage to use the same move twice in one combo. [i]Rising Rage Rx1 M1 Reset (Getup)[/i] Star Rage stands next to a ragdolled opponent and uses Garuda Rebound Slow. Use Rising Rage Rx1 on getup, and when Garuda Rebound returns (right after the second hit of rising rage Rx1) she should flick away from her opponent and cancel Rising Rage, which keeps them in stun long enough to reach them with her M1s. Gives Star Rage an M1 reset at the cost of only Garuda Rebound. Rising Rage is refunded and can be used again. This can be implemented into a combo after Garuda Stab R, but is very risky and conditional. [i]Rising Rage Rx1 M1 Reset (Uppercut)[/i] Star Rage uppercuts her opponent, steps forward slightly while using Garuda Rebound Slow as soon as possible. Her first kick of Rising Rage Rx1 is timed to hit her opponent as they are falling back down to her, and Garuda Rebound First Use is flicked away to cancel the move, allowing for an M1 reset. Gives Star Rage an M1 reset at the cost of only Garuda Rebound. Rising Rage is refunded and can be used again. [i]Rising Rage Rx2 M1 Reset[/i] Star Rage uppercuts her opponent, and uses Garuda Rebound Slow. Rising Rage Rx2 is used immediately, and Garuda Rebound is flicked away from her opponent as soon as it returns back to her. This allows her to front dash to her opponent and get M1s in, as well as refunding Rising Rage. Gives Star Rage an M1 reset at the cost of only Garuda Rebound. Rising Rage is refunded and can be used again, and is the easiest M1 Reset in her kit. [i]Double Mass Breaker[/i] Star Rage downslams her opponent, and uses Garuda Rebound away from her opponent. She hits her opponent with Mass Breaker on getup, and Garuda Rebound Second Use is kicked in the direction of where the opponent went. The opponent gets flung back towards her, allowing her to continue the combo. Gives Star Rage a high damage combo option with similar damage to one of the Rising Rage M1 resets. Use case is when Rising Rage is on cooldown and the opponent does not have evasive. [i]Garuda Rebound Uppercut Confirm[/i] Star Rage uppercuts her opponent, steps foward while immediately using Garuda Rebound. To activate the variant, she must press R as soon as Garuda Rebound hits the opponent. This makes it completely red, and can be done with a surf for style. Very situational option that can come in handy if conditions are met. Star Rage must have full Mass Buildup bar, only Garuda Rebound off cooldown, and opponent must not have evasive. Usually done for style. [i]Garuda Stab Ragdoll Manipulation[/i] Star Rage uses Garuda Stab on her opponent, and shiftlocks in the opposite direction on the second hit, which makes them not launch as far. The timing changes depending on the ping of her opponent. Very situational tech used to extend into Rising Rage or into an M1 Reset. Garuda Rebound Launch Star Rage kicks Garuda Rebound's Second Use directly above her opponent, launching them high into the air, allowing her to continue the combo. Very situational tech used to extend into Rising Rage, Garuda Stab or Mass Breaker. Also one of the only red transitions from Garuda Rebound into Mass Breaker. [i]Garuda Rebound Downslam Confirm[/i] Star Rage does three m1s on her opponent before quickly kicking Garuda Rebound's charged variant and follows up with a side dash downslam. Very situational tech that gives a quick confirm into Garuda Rebound's charged variant. This can also be used to bait evasive since it gives i-frames.

As stated, these are simpler as they are less executionally demanding than the techier ones. Simple Bread and Butter combo to safely convert off ragdoll and hit. Only costs you two moves. Not only can Star Rage leverage insane mixups and neutral applications, but generally speaking, they have the option to literally duplicate their abilities and their cooldown, providing with pressure and most importantly, options upon variants. Mastering the tech takes times, but it is unarguably crucial in order to turn this character from a normal M1 trader with some passivity, into a combo boss demon that punishes the life out of whoever was confident enough to risk their entire health bar.

You have the advantage because of your diverse options and ability to punish the heck out of Perfection. Just don't get caught by the front dash of blade mode. During an M1 trade, when in doubt, use aerial mass breaker.

One of the funnest mirror matchups. If both of you use Garuda Rebound during neutral, there will be a lot of parry exchanges at the high level that end up turning Jujutsu Shenanigans into Blade Ball. Winning comes down to whoever messes up their own neutral, by whiffing a neutral option or simply making a mistake during M1 trading.

Good luck being able to do anything after the R special gets popped on you. All of your moves and most variants get countered easily, including Garuda Rebound. However, the advantage that Star Rage has are minimal but crucial. Star Rage is able to Counter Bait the Aspiring Mangaka which allows you to punish the insane endlag effectively: - Whiffing Garuda Rebound - Whiffing Mass Breaker - Whiffing the first hit of 4+R - 3 + R - 4 + R If you do get inflicted with Aspiring Mangaka's R special, you have the ability to use mass breaker in the air as a mid safe M1 trading tool, but watch out for the counter again (and don't miss your 3)!

Against a competent Lucky Coward, every single one of your moves is easily dodged. Your combos are pointless because of Sword Off Mode, and this is just going to suck the life out of you. Tip? Try to whiff and feint your moves. Play really weirdly, and maybe... JUST maybe, you are able to capitalize. Lucky Coward's low health means even one mistake is incredibly costly, especially with your scary combos, but the issue here is that most of your combos are easily evasive punishable against a character who has evasives all the time. Intentionally overpowered boss character that can utterly curbstomp any of the vanilla cast in a 1v1. However, Heian Sukuna isn't playable outside of private/custom servers with Overpowered turned on and Final Showdown, meaning that in most cases, you'll be dealing with entire crowds as opposed to single targets. *Health scales with amount of players in Roulette server.

At a basic level Strongest of History can really just use any move over and over again mindlessly besides Open Furnace and get results, but the Strongest of History should be trying to make distance to use certain moves and build up his incantations.

Whenever possible, Strongest of History wants to use his R special to build up his incantations. Any of Strongest of History's incantation-boosted Strong Dismantles are usable, but the most viable ones typically go like this from strongest to weakest. Dismantle Net -> Dismantle Barrage -> World Cutting Slash -> Disgraced Sovereign Dismantle Net is even stronger than Open Furnace in lethality, so Strongest of History can use Cleave Rush to space himself and then fire it with no consequences. Dismantle Barrage is a great tool to space himself as well, and does great damage of course. It can be led into an Open Furnace or Dismantle Net with minimal risk. World Cutting Slash is similar to Dismantle net, although due to its much more minimized range and requiring Strongest of History to aim, it will be less viable in more situations, though if the Strongest of History is skilled it is basically interchangable with Dismantle Barrage. Disgraced Sovereign due to its low damage output and pitiful AOE (for a character like Strongest of History) is not as good as the other incantation-boosted Dismantles. In most cases, you are better off using Dismantle Barrage. But it does look cool, so that's something it has going for it.

Strongest of History has a black flash variant within Cleave Rush that is easily timeable. If the Strongest of History has played any Vessel you will remember the approximate 0.33 second timing to perform a black flash, which Strongest of History shares. Once you know this it becomes extremely easy to chain black flashes with this character. Black Flash is used at its best when there are large masses of enemies approaching, which is quite common. Strongest of History can produce this situation rather easily by just using a Dismantle Barrage. After each Black Flash you can backdash and continue to chain to keep yourself safe. Keep note that after Black Flashing you have little to no endlag, which does provide Strongest of History with an ounce of combo game, if you want to take out important targets.

Strongest of History should [u]never[/u] use Incomplete Shrine when he is close to a crowd. It is always more favorable to distance yourself, at least a bit, before popping your Incomplete Shrine. However, if Strongest of History [i]does[/i] successfully get their Incomplete Shrine off, it is easy to capitalize. Incomplete Shrine will constantly leave enemies on one-tap, which means you can fire Dismantle Barrages or Dismantle Nets to clean up. The added flexibility of having your domain opened also gives you the opportunity to build up a Dismantle Net for right when the domain ends.
